impurity

/im-PYOOR-ih-tee/ - the stress falls on PYOOR · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Impurity means a trace of a contaminating substance.

The assay listed every impurity in the well water by parts per billion, from iron down to a whisper of arsenic.

Worked Example

Museum conservators studying the medieval stained glass found that its famous rose color was no recipe at all but an accident: an impurity of gold dust, carried into the melt from a careless crucible, scattered light in a way no pure glass could. Some contamination, it turns out, is beautiful.

Impurity is more precise than dirt or flaw: it names a foreign trace mixed into a substance that should be all one thing - and it stays neutral about the result. A flaw is always bad; an impurity is simply not supposed to be there, whether it ruins the batch or, once in a century, improves it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

contaminant: A contaminant is whatever pollutes - bacteria in the water, fumes in the air - and the word is chosen for the harm it threatens, at any amount. An impurity is defined by belonging elsewhere, not by damage: a foreign trace in a substance meant to be all one thing, sometimes harmless.

taint: A taint is a corrupting trace that spoils by association, and it is often figurative - a taint of scandal, of suspicion, of doubt. An impurity is literal and physical: measurable foreign matter mixed into a substance, and the word passes no judgment at all on its own.

flaw: A flaw is a defect in the thing itself - a crack in the casting, a hole in the argument - present in how it was made or shaped rather than added from outside. An impurity is the opposite case: the substance is fine, but foreign matter has slipped in.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

purity: freedom from any foreign trace

clarity: clearness through and through

Where it sits · how unwanted and damaging the presence is — trace → impurity → pollutant

trace vs. impurity: A trace is just a tiny amount of anything, welcome or not; an impurity is a trace that does not belong.

pollutant vs. impurity: A pollutant goes beyond an impurity: impurities are unwanted traces inside a substance, while a pollutant fouls whole rivers and skies at damaging scale.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — im-

Prefix — im-: not

Root — pur-

Root — pur-: clean (Latin purus)

Suffix — -ity

Suffix — -ity: state of being

Put it together

Put it together: Im- (not) + pur- (Latin purus, 'clean') + -ity (the state of being) = the state of not being pure. This is the unit's suffix working in plain sight: pure is a living English adjective, impure its negative, and -ity turns it into a noun - which English then made countable, so a single speck of the not-pure is 'an impurity.'

Use the root in a new word: purify

Use the root in a new word: purify: Hikers purify creek water with a filter pump before they dare drink it.

Word Choice

neutral / technical

Impurity is the laboratory's word - assays, datasheets, and refining reports all use it for a foreign trace in a substance. Choose contaminant when you stress harm, taint when the corruption is figurative, and flaw when the defect is not foreign matter at all.
